title: Aaditya Personal Website
description: This portfolio itself — a component-based Next.js site with a typed content layer, a persisted light/dark theme, and Framer Motion animations throughout, built to be the front door to everything else here.

title: Excel Schema Diff
description: A reconciliation tool for matching member records between an internal system and an external consultant feed, where the same fields arrive under different headers and formats. The mapping table drives everything, so onboarding a new data source means editing a spreadsheet, not the code — a direct extension of the operations automation work behind Blumont's annuity data pipelines.

title: The Market Watcher
description: A full-stack stock price tracker with a Swagger-documented REST API pulling live quotes from the Twelve Data API, plus a lightweight frontend for searching symbols and reviewing recent lookups — a small bet on the fintech and markets side of software.

title: 2026 FIFA World Cup Bracket Predictor
description: The most complex logic I've shipped in a single file: a full 48-team, 12-group bracket predictor with drag-and-drop group ranking, third-place wildcard selection, and a knockout bracket where every pick cascades automatically through the rest of the tournament. Zero dependencies, state persisted to localStorage.

title: Math Games Arcade
description: Six classic browser games — 2048, Snake, Memory Match, Math Sprint, Tic-Tac-Toe with a minimax CPU, and Breakout — built in one dependency-free HTML file with a shared dark neon theme and persisted best scores. More about range and polish than any single hard problem.

title: LucidFlow Budget
description: A personal budgeting stack with a Flask + SQLAlchemy API backed by SQLite, and a dashboard that visualizes income, expenses, and net investments through a live Plotly Sankey diagram. The deepest technical dive of the group, from data model to chart rendering.
